title: The tree by the water
hookLine: blessed is the one like a tree planted by rivers of water (Psalm 1)
tomorrow: under a sky full of stars, how small is one person?

lines: A TREE PLANTED BY THE RIVERS.
cards: Keep a houseplant alive long enough and the secret turns out not to be the leaves. It's the water. So the first psalm compares a good life to a tree.

Psalm 1, in the King James Version: "And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither." A tree, yes. But look where it's planted.

teach.b: The verse just before says what the water is: "But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night." The Hebrew word for law there is torah: teaching.
And the Talmud tells a story about a young man who wanted that water badly.

teach.h: HILLEL ON THE ROOF, IN THE SNOW.
teach.b: Hillel was poor. Each day he paid part of his small wage to the guard at the house of study. One winter day he earned nothing, and the guard wouldn't let him in.
So he climbed onto the roof and lay across the skylight, to hear the teachers Shemaya and Avtalyon. Snow fell, and covered him. At dawn the teachers noticed the room was dark.
They looked up, and there was a man buried in snow across the window. They brought him down, washed him, and warmed him by the fire, though it was the Sabbath, saying he was worth it.
Jewish tradition makes the link outright.
The Talmud compares Torah to water, reading Isaiah's call, every one that thirsts, come to the waters, as a call to study.
Jewish tradition asks for study every day, and Hillel grew into a teacher whose sayings Jews still repeat.
The tree in Psalm 1 doesn't try harder in a dry year. Its roots already reached the river.

how: Jews study Torah as a lifelong, daily practice, often with a partner or in a class; Psalm 1 opens the Book of Psalms, which Jews and Christians both pray.

games.q: what does “the tree by the water” mean?
o: a person who stays the same and never changes
a life rooted in what feeds it, like a tree by a river
a family tree traced back through many generations

games.q: the tree and the roof: tap the pairs.
p: planted by the rivers of water
Torah, delighted in day and night
lay on the skylight in the snow
the teachers he climbed up to hear

s: Psalm 1 promises good people will never have a hard year
the tree still has seasons; what it has is water at its roots.
in the Talmud's story, Hillel was found under snow on the skylight
he climbed up to hear Shemaya and Avtalyon when he couldn't pay to get in.
the tree's strength in Psalm 1 comes from how hard it tries
the strength comes from where it's planted: by the rivers of water.

games.q: you're Hillel. you have no coin today, and the guard won't let you into the house of study. what do you do?
o: go home and try again tomorrow, when you've earned something.
climb onto the roof and listen through the skylight.
ask the guard to let you in this once, on credit.
games.why: Hillel climbed to the skylight to hear, and snow covered him. the teachers found him at dawn and warmed him by the fire.

practice: If you can, sit near a tree or a plant, or by a window with one in view. Put a hand on the bark or a leaf, or hold a glass of cool water and feel its weight, then take one slow sip.
Let the rest of the sit be roots: still, quiet, drawing water.

wordCard.voice: The tree by the water: Psalm 1's picture of a life rooted in what feeds it; for Jewish readers, Torah, studied day and night.

orig.note: Hebrew, from Psalm 1:3: streams of water, the rivers the tree is planted by.

carryVoice: For the road: by the rivers, where the roots drink. The Psalms are open, one day in.
